cast_dialogue.linea: We all carry a museum inside, heroes. 'Used to' is the key that opens the room of past habits.
I used to live in a small village, and I used to ride my bike to school every day.
I didn't use to speak English at all. Now I use it every day with you!
I used to have long hair. Did you use to play football, Ben?
I used to dance tango every weekend. Those days are gone, but the memories still dance with me.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Use 'used to + verb' for past habits and states that are NOT true now. In negatives and questions the 'd' disappears: 'didn't use to', 'Did you use to...?'.

filas: I didn't use to like vegetables.
I used to have long hair, but now it's short.

guion: Sofía: Did you use to live in the city, Ben?
Ben: No, I used to live in a small village. I used to ride my bike to school.
Sofía: That sounds nice! I used to have long hair in those days.
Ben: Really? I can't imagine that!
Sofía: And Kenji didn't use to speak English at all.
Ben: Wow. People change a lot!
Sofía: Yes, but Abuela Carmen still dances tango. Some things never change.
